rules.title: Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482) statewide rent increase cap
rules.requirement: Owners may not raise gross rent over any 12-month period by more than 5% plus regional CPI, or 10%, whichever is lower. The base is the lowest rent charged in the prior 12 months, and no more than two increases are allowed per 12 months. Rent may be reset on a new tenancy where no prior tenant remains. State law also requires 30 days' written notice for increases under 10%. Enforced by tenant civil action (overcharge damages, up to treble for willful conduct) and by the AG, city attorney or county counsel.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property statewide, including mobilehome park units, unless covered by stricter local rent control or otherwise exempt.
rules.exemptions: Housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; owner-occupied duplexes (neither unit an ADU/JADU); separately alienable single-family homes and condos not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, where the exemption notice was given; units under stricter local rent control; mobilehome homeowners.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The single-family/condo exemption requires a non-corporate owner and written exemption notice. Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing and dormitories are excluded.

rules.conflict_note: Originally enacted by AB 1482, effective 2020-01-01, and applicable to increases on or after 2019-03-15 (mobilehomes 2021-02-18). The current text from SB 567 (Stats. 2023, ch. 290) is operative 2024-04-01. The section is repealed 2030-01-01. The 30-day notice rule (from c110) is summarized without a statutory citation.

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act statewide just cause eviction requirement
rules.requirement: After 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy (24 months for one tenant if adult tenants were added), the owner may terminate only for an enumerated at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the written notice. Curable violations require notice and an opportunity to cure. For no-fault terminations the owner must pay relocation assistance equal to one month's rent within 15 calendar days, or waive the final month's rent. Owners must give tenants a 12-point statutory notice of the rent cap and just cause protections. Noncompliant termination notices are void.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property in California, including mobilehome park units, after 12 months of tenancy. Displaced where a qualifying local just cause ordinance applies.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; nonprofit hospitals and care facilities; dormitories; tenant shares bath or kitchen with a resident owner; owner-occupied single-family home renting up to two units or bedrooms; owner-occupied duplexes; certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; non-corporate-owned separately alienable units with notice; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires 12 or 24 months of occupancy. The separately-alienable-unit exemption requires non-corporate ownership plus written notice. Deed-restricted affordable housing is excluded.

rules.conflict_note: Original Tenant Protection Act just cause rules date from 2020. The current text is operative 2024-04-01 and was amended by AB 1529 effective 2026-01-01. The section is repealed 2030-01-01.

rules.title: Housing Crisis Act relocation for lower-income households displaced by demolition
rules.requirement: Lower-income households displaced by demolition of protected units for new housing must receive relocation benefits equal to those required of public entities under Gov. Code § 7260 et seq.
rules.coverage_conditions: Lower-income (80% AMI or below) households in protected units demolished for new housing development.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: RESTRICTED: lower-income households in protected units demolished for new housing development.

rules.citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6(b)(4)(A) (SB 330, as amended by SB 8 and AB 1218)
rules.conflict_note: In Los Angeles, the higher of the HCA or city amounts applies.

rules.title: Security deposit cap and handling (Civ. Code § 1950.5, AB 12)
rules.requirement:
Security, however denominated, may not exceed one month's rent in addition to first month's rent. Qualifying small landlords may charge two months, except to service members. Security may not be labeled nonrefundable. Handling requirements:
- Offer a pre-move-out initial inspection.
- Deduct only unpaid rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, and cleaning to move-in condition.
- Take photos at move-in (tenancies from 2025-07-01) and at move-out before and after repairs (from 2025-04-01).
- Return the balance with an itemized statement and receipts within 21 days.
- Return electronically if rent was paid electronically.
- Return any extra service-member security after 6 months.
Bad-faith retention exposes the landlord to up to 2x the deposit plus actual damages.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords); 21-day return
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental agreements in California. The cap applies to security demanded or collected on or after 2024-07-01.
rules.exemptions: Small landlords (natural persons or LLCs of natural persons owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total) may charge up to two months' rent, except to service members.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The small-landlord exception depends on the statewide portfolio and ownership form.

rules.conflict_note: The one-month cap (AB 12) took effect 2024-07-01. The prior limits were 2 months unfurnished and 3 months furnished. Subsidiary provisions took effect later: move-out photos and proof of repairs 2025-04-01/2025-01-01, move-in photos 2025-07-01, and electronic return (AB 414) 2026-01-01.

rules.title: Application screening fee cap and conditions
rules.requirement:
A screening fee may not exceed actual out-of-pocket cost and may not exceed $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted from 1998 ($68.96 for 2026). No fee may be charged if no unit is or will soon be available. A fee is allowed only under one of two processes:
- First-come, first-qualified review against written criteria, refunding applicants not considered.
- Full refund to non-selected applicants within 7 days of selection or 30 days of submission.
The landlord must give an itemized receipt and a copy of the credit report within 7 days, and refund unused portions.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and agents charging residential rental applicants, including guarantors and cosigners.
rules.exemptions: Does not preempt fee rules of federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.conflict_note: The original effective date is not stated in the corpus. The latest amendment is AB 1170, effective 2026-01-01. The first-qualified/refund process appears to reflect 2024 amendments effective 2025-01-01.

rules.title: FEHA source-of-income discrimination ban and subsidy-holder screening limits
rules.requirement:
Owners may not discriminate based on source of income, including Section 8 and VASH vouchers, and may not maintain 'No Section 8' policies. For applicants with a government rent subsidy:
- Income standards must be based only on the tenant's portion of rent.
- Credit history may be used only if the applicant is offered the option to provide verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay.
Income standards must count the aggregate income of co-residents.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of housing accommodations in California.
rules.exemptions: An owner-occupant renting to one additional person is exempt from certain FEHA housing provisions. Inquiring about level or source of income is not by itself discrimination.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The subsidy-related screening limits apply only to applicants with a government rent subsidy.

rules.conflict_note: SB 329 extended source of income to housing subsidies effective 2020-01-01. The SB 267 credit-history and income-standard provisions are in the current text effective 2024-01-01.

rules.title: FEHA / Civil Rights Council limits on criminal history screening
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not use blanket bans on people with criminal histories. They may not consider arrests not leading to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy safety, considering the nature and severity of the offense and the time elapsed.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most housing providers and tenant screening companies in California.
rules.exemptions: An owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act; Civil Rights Council criminal history housing regulations
rules.conflict_note: The specific CCR section is not cited in the corpus.

rules.title: AB 325 Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute one while coercing another to adopt its recommended price or terms. A common pricing algorithm is one used by two or more persons that relies on competitor data. The ban applies to rental housing as general antitrust law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person using, distributing, selling or licensing a common pricing algorithm in California, including landlords and rental software vendors.
rules.exemptions: End consumers; single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires use of a common pricing algorithm as part of an agreement to restrain trade, or coercion.

rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rules.conflict_note: The effective date is inferred from the default rule; the bill was chaptered 2025-10-06. This is a general antitrust statute, not housing-specific.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance rent ceilings and Annual General Adjustment
rules.requirement: For fully covered units, rent increases are limited to the Annual General Adjustment (AGA). The AGA is 65% of Bay Area CPI, capped at 5% by Measure BB; the 2026 AGA is 1.0%, effective no earlier than 2026-01-01. Landlords may use banked AGAs up to the rent ceiling. Capital improvement petitions are allowed only for completed improvements. For tenancies starting on or after 2024-02-06, utilities may be charged only in base rent or if separately metered in the tenant's name.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most units in multifamily properties with a certificate of occupancy on or before June 1980. Also single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996, rooming houses, and many subsidized units.
rules.exemptions: New construction with a CO after June 1980 (partially covered, no rent ceiling); most single-family homes and condos with tenancies from 1996 onward; Section 202/811 and HUD-insured project units; Golden Duplexes; owner shared kitchen/bath units; owner-occupied ADU properties; dorms; nonprofit cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Single-family homes and condos are covered only if the tenancy began before 1996. Coverage of subsidized units depends on subsidy type and HUD mortgage status. Golden Duplex, shared kitchen/bath and ADU owner-occupancy exemptions apply. The 2026 AGA excludes tenancies from 2025-01-01 onward with Costa-Hawkins-set rents.

rules.citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76 (incl. § 13.76.110A), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024); Rent Board Reg. 1148
rules.conflict_note: City sources describe the cutoff both as 'built before 1980' and as 'Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980'; the cutoff encoded here is a CO on or before 1980-06-30. Measure BB (Nov. 2024) amended the ordinance, and its effective date is not stated.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
rules.requirement:
Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for an enumerated just cause. Measure BB added these limits:
- No nonpayment eviction for debt under one month's HUD Fair Market Rent.
- No eviction for refusing a substantially similar new lease.
- Lease-breach evictions require actual harm and unreasonable conduct.
Termination notices must reference the Rent Board, and notices and complaints must be filed with the Board within 3 business days. A notice of tenant rights is due within 15 days of tenancy start (tenancies from 2024-12-20). Owner move-in and Ellis Act evictions require relocation assistance of $19,413, plus $6,471 for qualifying households (2026, CPI-indexed annually).
rules.coverage_conditions: All fully and partially covered units, including new construction, single-family homes, condominiums and subsidized units.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplexes (owner-occupied since 1979); units where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with the resident owner; tenancies after 2018-11-07 on owner-occupied ADU properties; university dorms; nonprofit cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemptions depend on owner occupancy (Golden Duplex, shared facilities, ADU), dorm status or cooperative status.

rules.citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76 (Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance), as amended by Measure BB; Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance
rules.conflict_note: Measure BB amendments date from Nov. 2024. The 2026 relocation amounts were approved 2025-10-16 and took effect 2026-01-01. Ellis relocation comes from the separate Ellis Implementation Ordinance at the same amounts.

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest
rules.requirement: Landlords of fully or partially covered units must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the end of each year, and a prorated amount on mid-year move-out.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully and partially covered units under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplexes; owner shared kitchen/bath units; owner-occupied ADU properties (tenancies after 2018-11-07); dorms; nonprofit cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemptions depend on owner occupancy and on dorm or cooperative status.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance (security deposit interest)
rules.conflict_note: The interest rate and code section are not stated in the corpus.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee rights notice and ban on non-refundable renewal fees
rules.requirement: Owners who charge a screening or credit report fee must first give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement, along with the Civ. Code § 1950.6(b) fee cap. Owners may not charge existing tenants non-refundable fees to renew a tenancy or to add, replace or remove roommates, regardless of lease terms.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners and agents of residential rental property in Berkeley.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or tenancy decisions. Any adverse action based on criminal history requires written notice and an opportunity to respond. The Notice to Rental Applicants must be posted on application materials.
rules.key_value: No criminal history inquiry or use
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing providers in Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner lives on site; lifetime sex offender registrants; limited public housing and Section 8 exemptions; owner move-back agreements; existing-tenant sublets and roommates.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemptions for lifetime sex offenders, public housing and Section 8, owner move-back agreements, and sublets or roommate additions.

rules.conflict_note: Passed by the City Council 2020-04-14; the effective date is not stated.

rules.title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm (one relying on nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old) to set rents or occupancy. No one may sell or license such algorithms to Berkeley landlords. Each unit-month is a separate violation, with civil penalties up to $1,000. The City Attorney and tenants may sue.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation (per unit per month)
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords of residential units in Berkeley, and vendors supplying them.
rules.exemptions: Aggregated or anonymous reports not recommending rents; affordable-housing rent/income limit tools; market research for financing, appraisal or software testing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a coordinated pricing algorithm using nonpublic competitor data is used.

rules.conflict_note: The ordinance was passed to print 2025-11-18 and adopted 2025-12-02, with no stated effective date. A secondary source gives January 2026, consistent with the 30-day rule. It amends existing BMC ch. 13.63. RealPage's challenge was dismissed with prejudice 2026-01-14.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance annual allowable increase
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, annual increases are limited to the Rent Board's allowable increase. The rate is 1.6% of base rent for 2026-03-01 through 2027-02-28.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled units under S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37.
rules.exemptions: Units first receiving a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979; Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies; some units whose rent is regulated by another agency.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Costa-Hawkins-exempt tenancies (e.g., single-family homes and condos) and agency-regulated units are excluded.

rules.conflict_note: The rate resets each March 1 (1.4% for 2025-26). The CO cutoff comes from the SF just cause overview (c178).

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction and relocation
rules.requirement:
Eviction from a covered unit requires one of 17 just causes that is the landlord's dominant motive. Lease expiration or a change of ownership is not just cause. Relocation payments for notices served 2026-03-01 to 2027-02-28:
- Owner/relative move-in, demolition, capital improvement or substantial rehab (§ 37.9C): $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 per elderly or disabled tenant or household with minor children.
- Ellis Act (§ 37.9A): $11,110.05 per tenant, max $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 per elderly (62+) or disabled tenant.
- Temporary capital-improvement displacement under 20 days (Civ. Code § 1947.9): $446 per day plus moving expenses.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance's eviction provisions, including post-1979 units and Costa-Hawkins tenancies.
rules.exemptions: Units not covered by the Rent Ordinance (not listed in the source).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The unit must be covered by the Rent Ordinance's eviction provisions.

rules.citation: S.F. Admin. Code §§ 37.9, 37.9A, 37.9C; Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9
rules.conflict_note: Relocation rates adjust each March 1. The archive dates § 37.9C rates to 2006-08-10.

rules.title: San Francisco security deposit interest
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the Rent Board rate. The rate is 4.2% for 2026-03-01 through 2027-02-28.
rules.coverage_conditions: Security deposits held for San Francisco rental units.
rules.citation: S.F. Admin. Code ch. 49 (security deposit interest)
rules.conflict_note: The ch. 49 citation is not stated in the source. Prior rates were 5.0% (2025-26) and 5.2% (2024-25).

rules.title: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance (affordable housing)
rules.requirement: Providers making affordable housing decisions may not unfairly use an applicant's or resident's arrest or conviction history.
rules.coverage_conditions: Affordable housing decisions in San Francisco.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: RESTRICTED: affordable housing providers and applicants.

rules.conflict_note: Agency landing page only; no code citation or effective date.

rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: The sale or use of algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor data to set rents or manage occupancy is prohibited. Tenants or the City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation. Each unit-month may be a separate violation.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential units in San Francisco.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a device using nonpublic competitor data is used.

rules.conflict_note: Approved by the Board of Supervisors in July 2024.

rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance allowable annual increase
rules.requirement: RSO rent may be raised once every 12 months by the LAHD allowable percentage (3% for 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30). Effective 2026-02-02, there is no added utility percentage and no 10% increase for an added dependent; 10% for an added non-dependent tenant remains. RSO and SCEP fees may be passed through after registration and notice. Larger increases require LAHD approval.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units in the City of Los Angeles first built or certified on or before 1978-10-01, plus LAMC 151.28 replacement units. Includes apartments, condos, duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on a parcel, ADUs and similar unit types.
rules.exemptions: Rent is unregulated for condo and townhome tenancies commenced after 1995-12-31. A single-family dwelling alone on a parcel is not covered. Luxury and temporary exemptions apply.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Replacement units are covered regardless of age. A single-family dwelling alone on a parcel is generally not covered. Condo/townhome tenancies after 1995 are rent-unregulated. Luxury and temporary exemptions apply.

rules.citation: LAMC Ch. XV, § 151.00 et seq. (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)
rules.conflict_note: LAHD describes coverage as 'first built on or before October 1, 1978'; the cutoff is encoded on the certificate of occupancy. The 3% figure expired 2026-06-30, and the allowable increase from 2026-07-01 onward (under the amended formula) is not stated in the corpus. The utility and dependent add-ons were eliminated 2026-02-02.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO just cause eviction and relocation
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO units may evict only for listed at-fault or no-fault reasons. Nonpayment evictions require arrears above one month's HUD Fair Market Rent (from 2023-03-27). No-fault evictions require filing a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice, plus relocation paid within 15 days. Relocation for 7/1/2026-6/30/2027: eligible tenants $11,000/$14,400; qualified tenants $23,150/$27,400; reduced Mom & Pop amounts for owner move-in. All termination notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days. Landlords must give the Notice of Renters' Protections (tenancies from 2023-01-27) and the Notice of Right to Counsel (from 2025-08-20).
rules.coverage_conditions: RSO units in the City of Los Angeles.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: RSO replacement units are covered regardless of age. A single-family dwelling alone on a parcel falls under the JCO instead. Relocation amounts depend on tenant age, disability, income and tenure.

rules.conflict_note: Relocation amounts adjust each July 1. Bulletin A says notice copies are due within 3 days and Bulletin B says within 3 business days.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (non-RSO units)
rules.requirement: For non-RSO units, after 6 months of tenancy or expiration of the original lease, landlords may terminate only for enumerated at-fault or no-fault reasons. The same Fair Market Rent nonpayment threshold and 3-business-day LAHD notice filing apply. No-fault terminations require relocation assistance at the RSO amounts, or one month's rent for a single-family home owned by a qualifying natural person. Separately, LAMC 47.06-47.07 require relocation for demolition or condo/commercial conversion regardless of RSO/JCO coverage.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential units in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO, including newer buildings and single-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; licensed care facilities; fraternity and sorority houses; owner's roommate; some cooperatives, nonprofit facilities and government-owned properties.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Also covers older non-RSO units, such as a single-family dwelling alone on a parcel. Requires 6 months of tenancy or lease expiration. Owner's-roommate and facility-type exceptions apply.

rules.citation: LAMC § 165.00 et seq. (Just Cause Ordinance), incl. §§ 165.03, 165.05.B.5, 165.06; LAMC §§ 47.06, 47.07
rules.conflict_note: The effective date is not stated in the corpus.

rules.title: Los Angeles Resident Protections Ordinance (demolition of Protected Units)
rules.requirement: Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for new construction must pay enhanced relocation to lower-income tenants. Standardized amounts for 7/1/2026-6/30/2027 are $115,480 (extremely low income), $96,750 (very low) and $87,450 (low). Tenants may remain up to 6 months before construction. Penalties start at $250,000 per displaced unit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Protected Units demolished for new construction. These include RSO units, units with recent affordability covenants or lower-income occupancy, and units Ellis-withdrawn in the past 10 years.
rules.exemptions: Households above low income receive only the RSO/JCO amounts.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: RESTRICTED: lower-income (80% AMI or below) households in Protected Units demolished for new construction.

rules.conflict_note: The source gives 2025-02-11 as both the adoption and effective date; the actual effective date may be later.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO security deposit interest
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO units must pay interest on security deposits at the annual City-set rate (4.320% for 2025). Interest is paid monthly or annually, by direct payment or rent credit, with written notice of the chosen method.
rules.coverage_conditions: RSO units in the City of Los Angeles.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The unit must be RSO-covered.

rules.conflict_note: Secondary source; the 2026 rate is not shown.

rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (just cause from start of tenancy)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy of more than 30 days without enumerated at-fault or no-fault just cause. Curable violations require a cure notice. No-fault terminations require relocation of 2 months' rent (3 months for seniors 62+ or disabled tenants), paid within 15 days or as a rent waiver. Displaced tenants have a 5-year right of first offer. Tenants must receive a 12-point protections notice and the SDHC guide. Buyouts must exceed the relocation amount and meet disclosure rules. Termination notices must be filed with SDHC within 3 business days once the SDHC portal is live.
rules.key_value: No-fault relocation: 2 months' rent (3 for seniors/disabled)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego, including mobilehome-park rentals, for tenancies over 30 days. Fixed-term leases of 3 months or less are excluded.
rules.exemptions: Transient and short-term rentals; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (Section 8 still covered); care and dorm facilities; shared kitchen/bath with a resident owner; owner-occupied single-family homes renting up to 2 units; owner-occupied two-unit structures; certificate of occupancy within 15 years; non-corporate-owned separately alienable units with notice.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The separately-alienable exemption requires a non-corporate owner and written notice. Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing is excluded.

rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7 (§§ 98.0701-98.0710; O-21647 N.S.)
rules.conflict_note: Amended by O-21769 N.S., effective 2024-03-28. The SDHC filing requirement (§ 98.0706(a)(2)) applies only 30 days after the portal launches, and the launch date is unverified.

rules.title: San Diego ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic devices relying on nonpublic competitor data to set rents or occupancy, and devices may not be sold or licensed to landlords. Tenants may sue for damages, injunctive relief and penalties up to $1,000 per violation. Each month and each property may be a separate violation.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Reports using aggregated data more than 90 days old or public data that do not recommend rates; affordable-housing compliance tools (per draft text).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a covered algorithmic device is used.

rules.conflict_note: The adopted ordinance text is not in the corpus. A secondary source reports it in force from June 2025. The Feb. 2025 draft (O-2025-107) was used only for exemptions.

rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance annual cap
rules.requirement: Rent may be raised once a year by no more than the lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change, with 0% if CPI is negative. The maximum is 2.87% for 2026-09-01 to 2027-08-31. Owners must give written notice of the ordinance and tenant rights at lease start and with any rent increase. Owners may petition for a fair-return increase.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental units in buildings constructed on or before 1995-02-01, and mobile home spaces offered for rent on or before 1990-01-01.
rules.exemptions: Buildings constructed after 1995-02-01; mobile home spaces first offered for rent after 1990-01-01.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Costa-Hawkins may further exempt single-family homes and condos (not stated by the city).

rules.conflict_note: No municipal code section is given.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days of tenancy, owners may terminate only for an enumerated just cause stated in a written notice, with a cure notice for curable violations. No-fault terminations require 3 months' relocation assistance or waiver of the final 3 months' rent. Owners must notify tenants of the ordinance's protections.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in Santa Ana lasting more than 30 days.
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotels and transient occupancy; hospitals and care facilities; dormitories; shared living quarters.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Deed-restricted affordable housing, transient occupancy, care facilities, dorms and shared quarters are excluded.

rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (2021)
rules.conflict_note: 'Housing produced in the last 15 years' does not specify construction versus CO date.

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing
rules.requirement: The sale, licensing, provision or use of algorithmic rent-setting software relying on nonpublic competitor data is prohibited for Santa Ana residential rentals. Tenants may sue for damages, injunctive relief and up to $1,000 per violation per month.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation per month
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in Santa Ana, and software vendors.
rules.exemptions: Software using only public or aggregate historical data; affordable-housing compliance tools.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where covered software is used.

rules.conflict_note: First reading was 2026-02-17 and final adoption about 2026-03-03. OCBJ implies effect in March 2026, while Morgan Lewis gives 2026-04-02, consistent with the 30-day rule.

rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance (Chapter 260)
rules.requirement: Rent increases on covered units are regulated by the Rent Control Ordinance, administered by the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations. Increases beyond standard CPI-based limits require application, such as for capital improvement or hardship. Tenants may file illegal-rent complaints.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental properties with 5 or more units in Jersey City.
rules.exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties. Other exemptions are available by Rent Control Exemption Request. Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from municipal rent control for 30 years after completion (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Ordinance exemptions granted by request; HUD-subsidized and NJHMFA-financed units are not subject to municipal rent control.

rules.conflict_note: The increase formula is not stated. The 30-year exemption comes from state law per the NJ DCA guide (c159).

rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent coordination services
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services, such as RealPage, that rely on nonpublic data. Enforcement is public and private, with fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential landlords in Jersey City.
rules.exemptions: Reportedly excludes real estate agents.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where an algorithmic rent coordination service is used.

rules.conflict_note: The NJ FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43, effective 2027-07-01) § 6(b) bars conflicting municipal ordinances and may preempt this ban. Sources are secondary.

rules.title: Hoboken ban on algorithmic rent coordination
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms to coordinate or recommend rents, lease terms or occupancy.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential landlords in Hoboken.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where covered software or platforms are used.

rules.conflict_note: The NJ FAIR Act § 6(b) may preempt conflicting municipal ordinances from 2027-07-01. The citation format is unverified.

rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act good-cause requirement
rules.requirement:
A residential landlord may not evict, or fail to renew a written or oral lease, without one of the statutory good causes, served with the required notices. Related protections:
- Illegal-occupancy evictions require relocation of 6x monthly rent.
- Self-help lockouts are illegal (N.J.S.A. 2A:39-1).
- Reprisal is barred (2A:42-10.10).
- Foreclosure is not grounds for eviction, and new owners must notify tenants within 10 business days (2A:50-69).
- Eligible senior and disabled tenants in conversions get up to 40 years of protected tenancy (2A:18-61.22).
- Landlords of buildings with more than 2 units must distribute the Truth in Renting statement (46:8-43).
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals in New Jersey, including single-family homes, apartments, mobile homes and rooming houses.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; transient or seasonal hotel/motel guests; units held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Transient/seasonal and trust-unit exemptions.

rules.title: No unconscionable rent increases
rules.requirement: There is no statewide numeric cap, but rent increases must not be unconscionable and must comply with municipal rent ordinances. An increase takes effect only after valid notice to quit and notice of increase. Rents may not be raised to cover costs resulting solely from a condo, co-op or fee-simple conversion.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units.
rules.conflict_note: New Jersey has no state rent control law; municipal ordinances may impose caps.

rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Act
rules.requirement: Deposits may not exceed 1.5 months' rent, including pet deposits and prepaid rent, and annual deposit increases are capped at 10%. Deposits must be held in an interest-bearing NJ account, with written bank notice within 30 days and interest paid annually. The deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions, must be returned within 30 days of termination (5 business days after a fire, flood or similar displacement). Wrongful withholding is subject to double damages.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant opts in; seasonal rentals of 125 days or less.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Seasonal-rental exemption; tenant opt-in for owner-occupied 2-3 family dwellings.

rules.title: NJ residential rental application fee cap
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an application or similar fee above $50. The cap is CPI-adjusted annually from 2027-01-01.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property other than units in one- or two-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: One- and two-family dwellings; Real Estate Commission licensees unless the licensee is the landlord.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The licensee exemption applies unless the licensee is the landlord.

rules.conflict_note: The effective date is computed from enactment on 2026-01-20 (first day of the fourth month following).

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about criminal records before a conditional offer, except about methamphetamine production on federally assisted premises or lifetime sex-offender registration. Arrests, expunged or sealed records and juvenile adjudications may never be considered. After an offer, only specified convictions within lookback periods may be considered (1st degree 6 years; 2nd/3rd 4 years; 4th 1 year; lifetime for listed crimes), with an individualized assessment. Advertisements excluding people with records and drug or alcohol testing of applicants are prohibited.
rules.key_value: No criminal inquiry before conditional offer
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers of rental dwelling units in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four units.
rules.conflict_note: The effective date is computed from approval on 2021-06-18 (first day of the seventh month following).

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or otherwise discriminate based on protected classes. These include the source of lawful income or rent payment (e.g., Section 8 vouchers), race, creed, sex, familial status, disability, gender identity and sexual orientation.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rentals of real property in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: One unit in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rooms in an owner-occupied one-family home; certain religious and age-restricted housing.

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Rental property owners and their agents may not pay for or use the services of a coordinator, meaning algorithmic revenue management software that uses competitors' nonpublic, competitively sensitive data to set or recommend rents, terms or occupancy. Coordinators may not facilitate anticompetitive agreements, perform coordinating functions or engage in parallel pricing coordination. Violations are violations of the NJ Antitrust Act, and the AG must set up a complaint portal.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental property owners in New Jersey, and software providers and coordinators.
rules.exemptions: Government affordability programs; research not used for pricing; free public rent estimates; equal-access brokerage databases that do not recommend prices; non-AI spreadsheets requiring human analysis.
rules.conflict_note: Approved 2026-07-20 and effective on the first day of the twelfth month following (2027-07-01). Section 6(b) prohibits conflicting municipal ordinances, which may preempt the Jersey City and Hoboken bans.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 statewide rent control (struck from 2026 ballot)
rules.requirement: The petition would have repealed G.L. c. 40P and capped annual increases at the lesser of CPI or 5%. The SJC barred it from the November 2026 ballot, so it is not law. Massachusetts has no rent cap, and c. 40P bars local rent control.
rules.key_value: Proposed: lesser of CPI or 5% (not law)
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental units statewide, as proposed.
rules.exemptions: Proposed: owner-occupied buildings of 4 or fewer units; units under 10 years old; certain public, short-term, educational, religious and nonprofit units.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Measure never took effect.

rules.citation: Initiative Petition 25-21; Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893 (2026)
rules.conflict_note: Decided 2026-06-23 because the religious exemption violated Article 48. A refiling is possible (proponents mention 2028).

rules.title: Massachusetts notice-to-quit requirements (no just-cause requirement)
rules.requirement: A tenancy at will may be ended on written notice of one rental period or 30 days, whichever is longer, up to a maximum of 3 months. Nonpayment requires a 14-day notice to quit. Tenants at will may cure within 10 days, once per 12 months; written-lease tenants may cure by the answer date. A 7-day continuance applies when nonpayment was caused by government payment delay. Nonpayment notices must include the state form on rental assistance (§ 31), or the court will not accept the filing.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in Massachusetts.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The right to cure depends on prior notices and on lease type.

rules.conflict_note: These are procedural notice rules; Massachusetts has no just-cause eviction statute.

rules.title: Massachusetts anti-retaliation protection
rules.requirement: Landlords may not retaliate against tenants for enforcing housing laws, reporting violations, complaining in writing or organizing. A termination notice (other than for nonpayment), rent increase or substantial change within 6 months of protected activity is presumed retaliatory. Damages are 1-3 months' rent or actual damages, plus fees.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenants in Massachusetts who engaged in protected activity.
rules.exemptions: The presumption does not apply to nonpayment termination notices.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Requires protected activity within the prior 6 months.

rules.title: Massachusetts security deposit law
rules.requirement:
A security deposit may not exceed one month's rent. Handling requirements:
- Hold the deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, with a receipt giving bank details within 30 days.
- Provide a statement of condition within 10 days.
- Pay 5% annual interest (or the bank rate, if lower).
- Return the deposit within 30 days after the tenancy ends, deducting only for unpaid rent and damage beyond normal wear and tear, with a sworn itemization.
- Transfer the deposit to any successor owner, who must give notice within 45 days.
A regulation-authorized optional fee in lieu of a deposit may be offered; fees plus deposit may not exceed one month's rent. Violations can mean forfeiture of the deposit and treble damages.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Excludes vacation tenancies of 100 days or less.

rules.conflict_note: The fee-in-lieu option depends on EOHLC regulations, whose status is unknown.

rules.title: Massachusetts limit on upfront charges (no application fees)
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a lessor or the lessor's agent may require only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent, and the cost of a new lock and key. Application and all other upfront fees are prohibited.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.
rules.conflict_note: The limit has been in place since the 1970s per a secondary source. St. 2025, c. 9 extended it to lessors' agents effective 2025-08-01.

rules.title: Massachusetts broker fee paid only by the hiring party
rules.requirement: A licensed broker may contract with either the tenant or the landlord, not both. Any fee may be paid only by the party that engaged the broker. Brokers must disclose fee terms in writing (254 CMR 7.00).
rules.key_value: Fee paid only by the party that hired the broker
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rentals in Massachusetts involving a licensed broker.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a licensed broker is involved.

rules.citation: M.G.L. c. 112, § 87DDD½, as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43
rules.conflict_note: The 254 CMR 7.00 disclosure detail comes from an archived secondary article.

rules.title: Massachusetts housing discrimination ban incl. public assistance and housing subsidy
rules.requirement: Rental providers may not discriminate against recipients of public assistance or housing subsidies (including vouchers), or because of program requirements. They also may not refuse to rent based on protected characteristics or children, or make inquiries about protected characteristics.
rules.coverage_conditions: Persons furnishing rental accommodations in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: The general protected-class and children provisions (§ 4(6), (7), (11)) exempt a unit in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling and certain small elderly-occupied dwellings. The subsidy provision (§ 4(10)) has no such exemption.

rules.title: H.5222 Act preventing algorithmic rent fixing (pending)
rules.requirement: A pending bill to prevent algorithmic rent fixing in the rental market. It is not law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts rental housing (bill text not provided).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Bill text unknown.

rules.conflict_note: Reported favorably 2026-03-12 and referred to House Ways and Means.

rules.title: S.2983 Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting (pending)
rules.requirement: A pending Senate bill to prohibit algorithmic rent setting. It is not law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts rental housing (bill text not provided).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Bill text unknown.

rules.conflict_note: Reported favorably 2026-03-12 and referred to Senate Ways and Means.

rules.title: Boston rent stabilization home rule petition (H.3744) - not enacted
rules.requirement: The petition would have authorized Boston rent stabilization. It was sent to a study order and not enacted, so Boston has no rent cap. G.L. c. 40P bars local rent control.
rules.coverage_conditions: Boston residential rentals, as proposed.
rules.conflict_note: Accompanied study order H5035 on 2024-09-09; the session ended without enactment.

rules.title: Boston tenant eviction protections home rule petition (H.3744) - not enacted
rules.requirement: The petition would have authorized Boston tenant eviction protections. It was not enacted, so there is no just-cause requirement from it.
rules.coverage_conditions: Boston residential tenancies, as proposed.
rules.conflict_note: Accompanied study order H5035 on 2024-09-09; not enacted.

rules.title: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: Landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy must give the City's Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources with the notice to quit or non-renewal. They must submit the notice and tenant contact information to the City's portal. The first offense draws a warning, then $300 per day. Violations do not halt the eviction, and the requirements cannot be waived.
rules.key_value: Notice with notice to quit; $300/day fine
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords and foreclosing owners ending tenancies in Boston.
rules.exemptions: Hospitals, skilled nursing and health facilities; nonprofit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Triggered only by a notice to quit or non-renewal.

rules.citation: Boston City Ordinances § 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.conflict_note: Passed October 2020. The § 10-11.7 citation is taken from the penalty table.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND-funded and IDP units)
rules.requirement: Covered providers may not use blanket criminal-record bans. They may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or juvenile records, or convictions older than 5 years. They may not use credit scores, may use credit history only in lieu of rental history, and may not reject applicants for lack of credit history alone.
rules.key_value: No convictions older than 5 years; no credit scores
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving DND funding or land, and BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy income-restricted units.
rules.exemptions: Direct relationship or substantial-risk cases; current criminal behavior; federal and state requirements.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: RESTRICTED: DND-funded or DND-land housing and BPDA IDP income-restricted units.

rules.citation: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Feb. 2017)
rules.conflict_note: An agency funding policy, not a codified ordinance.

rules.title: Boston fair housing ban on rental assistance discrimination
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate based on rental assistance, such as refusing Section 8 or veterans vouchers, or based on other protected classes. The Boston Fair Housing Commission enforces this.
rules.coverage_conditions: Renting housing in Boston.
rules.citation: Boston fair housing law enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission
rules.conflict_note: No ordinance citation is given; the protection may derive from M.G.L. c. 151B.

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance (incl. source of income)
rules.requirement: Landlords and agents may not discriminate in renting, viewing or tenancy terms based on protected categories, including source of income such as Section 8 and public benefits. Reasonable uniform standards, such as ability to pay, are allowed.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing in Cambridge.
rules.exemptions: Two-family dwellings where the owner lives in the building.

rules.title: Cambridge Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance
rules.requirement: Owners, landlords and managers must give tenants the City's Tenants Rights and Resources Guide at the start of a tenancy and when taking steps to terminate it (notice to quit or summary process). The fine is $300 per day.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Cambridge, including tenancies at will.
rules.exemptions: Hospital and health facilities; nonprofit short-term substance abuse treatment; short-term rentals.
rules.conflict_note: A notice requirement only; it does not restrict eviction grounds.
